title: Two sticks (Ezekiel 37:15–28)
hookLine: the sticks of Judah and Joseph become one in the prophet's hand

lines: ONE FOR JUDAH, ONE FOR JOSEPH.
cards: Two sticks. That's all Ezekiel needs for today's message. No vision this time, no fire, no wheels.

He's told to write a name on each one. On the first: For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions. On the second: For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions.
Two names that stood for the two kingdoms, south and north, and the north had been carried off and scattered. And then he's told to hold them.

teach.h: WRITE A NAME ON EACH STICK.
teach.b: Here's the instruction, in the King James words: "And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand."
From where the people stand: two sticks, end to end, held in one fist, the prophet's hand closed around the seam. It's street theater, meant to make people ask.

So the text gives them their question: wilt thou not shew us what thou meanest by these? And the answer: God will take the stick of Joseph and join it with the stick of Judah, and they shall be one in mine hand.
Notice the shift. First, one in thy hand, the prophet's. Then, one in mine hand, God's.
In the text, the prophet's small act pictures something God says he will finish. Then the promise is spelled out. The scattered will be gathered from among the nations and brought home.

teach.h: THEY SHALL BECOME ONE IN THINE HAND.
teach.b: They shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all.
One king. One people. A covenant of peace, and God's dwelling place with them.
Remember the north falling, a few weeks back, its people carried off to Assyria.
Here a prophet says the story isn't over. Jewish tradition carries the hope of gathering the scattered in its prayers.
And the image also works at kitchen-table size: two people who stopped speaking, two halves of a family, two parts of yourself that don't get along. The prophet doesn't glue the sticks.
He holds them together in his hand, and waits for the rest.

how: Jews read Ezekiel 37:15–28 as the prophetic reading for the Torah portion Vayigash, where Joseph and Judah meet, and the hope of gathering the scattered appears in daily prayer.

games.q: you're Ezekiel, holding two sticks with two names on them. what are you told to do?
o: join them into one stick in your hand.
games.why: he joins them so they become one in his hand, and then God says: they shall be one in mine hand.

practice: If there are two pens or spoons nearby, pick them up; if not, just open your hands, and bring to mind two things split apart: two people, two sides of a family, two parts of your own life.
Let one rest in each hand, then slowly bring your hands together and hold them as one, without solving anything. If you pray, you can place them in God's hand.

wordCard.voice: Two sticks. Ezekiel writes Judah on one and Joseph on the other, and holds them so they become one in his hand: a promise that the divided will be joined. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: wood, or a stick, the word Ezekiel writes the names on.

carryVoice: Your line: one in thy hand. Then, one in God's hand, as the text promises. Until tomorrow.
